text:
maya: Quick sync 152 15 about pool quota UX. Dropped a Figma link with a new non-blocking suggestion banner and refined stepper behavior. PTAL: https://www.figma.com/file/yyy/autoscale-quota-banner kevin: skimmed it. banner looks good but question: should the banner auto-suggest values or just explain the conflict? testers got confused when tools changed fields automatically before. olivia: strong +1 on not changing user input silently. prefer: show suggestion buttons (Apply / Dismiss) and keep user's current values until they click apply. Banner must be reachable via keyboard and announced to screen readers. sam: UX note from research: users expect the banner to surface a quick action that resolves the issue with one click. If we show 2 suggestions (auto-shrink max or bump min), label them clearly: "Lower max to pool limit (8)" and "Increase min to pool min (2)". jordan: technical/accessibility: implement as role="alertdialog" when it includes action buttons so screen readers move focus into it. If it's purely informative, role="status" or role="alert" is fine. Also ensure focus trap only when necessary. maya: good differentiation. I think we only trap focus when a required change is mandatory. For non-blocking suggestions we should set tabindex="-1" on banner and move focus there briefly so SR users are aware, but don't trap. kevin: stepper behavior: current stepper snaps by 2s when users hold arrow. That's been tripping people up. Let's change to step=1 on keyboard arrow and accelerate only after 500ms hold. Also add hover + click drag support for precision. olivia: contrast check: the small hint under the pool chip ("supports burst") is 2.8:1. Need to bring to 3:1 at least. Also ensure the chips themselves are keyboard focusable and announce content like "pool alpha, region us-west, A100". sam: adding copy suggestions for banner text: "Selected pool 'alpha-usw' allows max 8 GPUs. Your Max (15) exceeds this. Suggested actions: Lower Max to 8 or pick a different pool." Keep it short. jordan: aria example for the suggested buttons inside banner: ```html

Selected pool max GPUs is 8; your Max (15) exceeds this.

``` maya: acceptance criteria draft: - Banner appears inline under pool selector when mismatched values detected - Banner uses role="alert" for simple notices, role="alertdialog" when action required - Banner receives focus (tabindex="-1" + focus()) and is reachable by keyboard - Suggested buttons are clear and keyboard operable - No silent mutation of user's inputs without explicit Apply - Stepper uses step=1, visible 4px focus ring, and aria-live updates for changes - Small badges on pool chips must be announced (e.g., "A100") - Contrast for helper text bumped to >=3:1 kevin: QA implications: when switching pools, test both directions: a) pool with higher quota -> preserve values, b) pool with lower quota -> banner appears and nothing auto-changes unless Apply clicked. sam can you add to test matrix. sam: yep will add. Also include keyboard-only flow: tab to pool, change, tab stops on banner, then Tab to suggested button; ensure SR reads the banner. olivia: copy tweak: change label "Pool" to "GPU pool" in the selector and add secondary text: "(region • GPU family)" so users see "alpha-usw (us-west • A100)". That reduces confusion. jordan: for stepper aria-live snippet: ```html Max capacity updated to 8 GPUs ``` kevin: on SLO controls: can we add a small inline toggle "Show cost impact" that when enabled displays micro-estimates under the slider? default off. Many users found inline numbers noisy during testing. maya: let's default it off and persist preference per-project. If enabled and cost >20% show modal before save. sam: QA will need scenarios for SLO with toggle on/off and cost modal firing. I'll create tickets. olivia: accessibility checklist reminder: all interactive bits (chips, steppers, banner buttons, modal) need role, label, and keyboard focus styles. I'll run a quick color + focus audit and post screenshots. maya: timeline: ship banner + stepper + chip badges this sprint. SLO cost toggle and modal next sprint. Kevin/jordan pair for the stepper implementation. Olivia/QA coordinate on audit and test cases. kevin: opening WIP PR now, adding notes. :hammer_and_wrench: maya: thanks everyone. closing with small follow-up: I'll add the final copy to Figma and pin the accessibility checklist in the file. design-bot: tag a11y review when ready. qa-bot: New QA task created: AUTOSCALE-4872 "Pool quota suggestion banner" assigned to sam. Link: https://jira.internal/browse/AUTOSCALE-4872
